detail: fe7_reachable renders the movement cost map with the WRONG STRIDE, producing a grid that is pure garbage, and fe7_act validates destinations against the same bad data. Chapter 1 Lyn HM, Lyn slot 0 at (13,7) per her unit struct. fe7_reachable reported "53 tiles, 53 legal destinations, max cost 6" and drew cost 0 at (18,2) — not where Lyn is, and outside the map (RAM.md: cursor stops at x=14, so width is 15). The rendered grid also had DISCONNECTED ISLANDS, which is impossible for a movement range and is the tell. Root cause, read from memory: the row-pointer table at 0x03000440 holds 14 pointers (0x03000478, 0x03000489, 0x0300049A, ... 0x03000555) then a 0xFFFFFFFF terminator. Consecutive pointers differ by 0x11 = 17, so the row stride is 17 bytes and there are 14 rows. src/fe7.ts uses GRID_W=24, GRID_ROWS=27, base A.gridData=0x030004AC — all three wrong. Correct decode, verified: base 0x03000478, stride 17, row index = y+2, column index = x with no offset. Decoding the raw 238 bytes that way puts cost 0x00 at row 9 col 13 = (13,7), exactly matching Lyn's struct position, and yields a properly connected 32-tile diamond (x8..x14, y3..y9) instead of 53 scattered tiles. The 24-stride read also runs off the end of the real buffer (0x030004AC + (y+2)*24 + x reaches 0x579 for tiles Lyn can legally reach; the grid data ends at 0x03000566), so it is reading unrelated IWRAM as movement cost.
wanted: Fix the three constants in src/fe7.ts: A.gridData = 0x03000478 (not 0x030004AC), GRID_W = 17 (not 24), GRID_ROWS = 14 (not 27); keep GRID_Y_OFF = 2, which is correct. Better still, stop hardcoding: read the row-pointer table at 0x03000440, walk it until 0xFFFFFFFF, and use pointer[y+2] as each row's base — that derives both the stride and the row count from the game and survives a map with different dimensions, which a hardcoded 17 will not. gridCost() should also bounds-check x against the real map width rather than GRID_W, since columns 15-16 of each row are padding. This is P0: fe7_act's destination validation is built on gridCost(), so right now every move is being validated against garbage.

detail: fe7_act reported a committed action as FAILED, on a map where the acting unit is the only deployed player unit. Chapter 1 Lyn HM, turn 1: fe7_act(slot 0, x 9, y 7, action 'wait') returned "Unit #0 MOVED to (9,7) but Wait did not commit after retries (+0x0C = 0x00). The action menu is probably still open." The action menu was NOT still open. Wait had committed fine. Because Lyn is the ONLY deployed player unit (players deployed 1/1), her Wait ended the player phase immediately; the enemy phase ran and the turn counter advanced to 2, which RESET every unit's has-acted flag. So fe7_act polled +0x0C, saw 0x00, and read "not yet acted" when the true meaning was "already acted, and the turn has since rolled over". fe7_unstick confirmed: phase 0x00 player, turn 2, selected unit none, verdict FREE CURSOR. The retry loop is what makes this dangerous rather than cosmetic — it kept pressing while the phase was flipping underneath it, and those presses landed during the enemy phase.
wanted: fe7_act should latch the turn counter (0x0202BC08) and phase byte (0x0202BC07) BEFORE it commits, and treat "turn advanced" or "phase left player" as SUCCESS rather than polling +0x0C to a timeout. Reading +0x0C == 0 is only evidence of failure if the turn is still the same turn — otherwise a cleared flag is exactly what success looks like. Concretely: after pressing the action, if turn != turnBefore || phase != 0x00, return success and say the phase ended. This will misfire on every single-unit map (all of Lyn ch.1) and on any map where the last unspent unit acts, which is once per turn on every map.

detail: fe7_act(action:'item') used the item successfully, then reported failure AND left the cursor sitting in the item submenu on "Discard." — one stray A from destroying an item. Chapter 1 Lyn HM turn 3: Lyn slot 0 at (8,6), 6/16 HP, inventory [01x43 Iron Sword, 6Bx3 Vulnerary, 6Bx3 Vulnerary]. Called fe7_act(slot 0, x 8, y 6, action 'item', item_slot 1). Return value: "Unit #0 selected item 6B but nothing committed. HP 6 -> 16. Text buffer: 'Discard.' Unit left unspent at (8,6)." Every part of that after the HP reading is wrong. The Vulnerary WAS used (HP 6 -> 16, a flat +10 as RAM.md documents), Lyn WAS spent, and because she is the only deployed unit that ended the player phase — fe7_unstick immediately after showed turn 4, phase 0x00, selected unit none, text buffer "Plain.", verdict FREE CURSOR. So the tool reported "nothing committed / left unspent" about an action that had both committed and rolled the turn over. Note the tool itself printed the evidence contradicting its own verdict: it reported "HP 6 -> 16" in the same sentence as "nothing committed". The dangerous part is the "Discard." text: the retry loop had navigated INTO the item submenu, where Use/Discard live. It stopped there and returned, but a further retry pressing A would have discarded a Vulnerary. This is the same underlying defect as the earlier fe7_act 'wait' false negative — polling the has-acted flag across a turn rollover — but the item path escalates it from a confusing message to potential item loss.
wanted: Two fixes. (1) Same as the 'wait' case: latch turn (0x0202BC08) and phase (0x0202BC07) before committing and treat a turn advance or phase change as SUCCESS, instead of polling +0x0C. (2) Make the item path fail CLOSED: if confirmation is ambiguous, press B to back out of the submenu rather than retrying A, and never retry A while the text buffer reads "Discard." — the retry loop should hard-abort on that string. Also worth having fe7_act cross-check the obvious effect it already has in hand: it read HP 6 -> 16 and still concluded nothing happened, so for action 'item' a changed HP (or a decremented item use count) should by itself be sufficient proof of commit.

detail: The chapter objective is "Seize gate" (read from the text buffer at 0x0202A5B4 via fe7_unstick) and there is NO way to find out where the gate IS. Chapter 1 Lyn HM: one enemy left, and the win condition is a tile I cannot locate. Nothing in the tool layer exposes terrain: fe7_state gives units only, fe7_reachable gives movement COST (which tells me a tile is enterable, not what it is), and fe7_forecast's +0x55 terrain ID only covers the two tiles involved in a specific forecast — I would have to forecast an attack from a tile to learn its terrain, which requires an adjacent enemy and so is useless for scouting an empty gate tile. RAM.md confirms the terrain/map tile array is still unlocated, and lists "Terrain ID -> name mapping" as open with only two known IDs (23 plain, 29 +1 Def/+20 Avo). My only remaining options are to walk Lyn onto candidate tiles and watch the cursor terrain readout, or read the gate's position off a screenshot — and the runbook forbids reading game state from pixels. So on a Seize map I can play the whole chapter correctly and still be unable to finish it, which is a hard blocker rather than an inconvenience.
wanted: Two things, in priority order. (1) [mem] Locate the terrain array. RAM.md already suggests the best lever: look for another row-pointer table shaped like the movement grid's — and note the movement grid's real shape is now known (table at 0x03000440, 14 pointers, stride 0x11, terminated by 0xFFFFFFFF), so that is a concrete template to pattern-match against rather than searching for terrain IDs blind. (2) [tool] Build fe7_terrain — an ASCII map of terrain IDs/names over the whole board, the same shape fe7_reachable prints, so "where is the gate" is one call. Failing the full array, a much cheaper stopgap that would unblock THIS chapter: fe7_objective, returning the objective string plus the seize/defend tile coordinates, since the game must store that tile somewhere to check the win condition. Also worth exposing the cursor's terrain-name readout (the string that renders bottom-left, e.g. "Plain") as a queryable per-tile lookup — fe7_unstick already reads that buffer incidentally, so a fe7_inspect(x,y) that parks the cursor and reports the terrain name would work today with no memory research at all.

detail: Severity escalation on the movement-grid stride bug: it can make the chapter objective UNREACHABLE, not just mis-drawn. Chapter 1 Lyn HM turn 5, Lyn slot 0 at (6,3) Move 5, last enemy a Brigand at (3,2). The four tiles adjacent to the brigand are (2,2), (4,2), (3,1), (3,3). Intersecting the TRUE cost map (decoded from 0x03000478, stride 17) against the BUGGY one fe7_act/fe7_forecast validate with (base 0x030004AC, stride 24) gives an EMPTY set: (4,2) cost 3, (3,3) cost 3 and (2,2) cost 5 are all genuinely reachable but the buggy grid marks them 0xFF and refuses; (3,1) is the only one the buggy grid accepts and it is genuinely out of range. Confirmed live — fe7_forecast(slot 0, x 4, y 2, target_slot 0) returned "Destination (4,2) is NOT reachable ... grid = 0xFF". So with one enemy left and a healthy lord I could not attack at all. Note this also means fe7_forecast validates against the same bad grid as fe7_act, so there is no read-only escape hatch. WORKAROUND USED, which is the reusable part: decode the real grid by hand (mgba_read_range at 0x03000478, 238 bytes, stride 17, row = y+2), decode the buggy render fe7_reachable prints, INTERSECT the two, and only ever pass fe7_act a tile legal under BOTH. Mutually-legal tiles from (6,3) were (5,0),(6,0),(7,0),(8,0),(10,2),(4,3),(7,6),(8,6),(7,7); I took (4,3) to close distance and will re-intersect next turn, since the buggy grid's shape shifts as the unit moves and may open an adjacent tile.
wanted: This is the same P0 fix already filed (A.gridData 0x03000478 / GRID_W 17 / GRID_ROWS 14, or better, walk the row-pointer table at 0x03000440) — filing this separately only to record that the bug is CHAPTER-BLOCKING rather than cosmetic, and that fe7_forecast is affected too and so cannot be used to work around fe7_act. Until it is fixed there is no in-tool workaround at all: the intersect trick above requires raw mgba_read_range plus manual decoding, which defeats the point of the fe7_* layer, and on an unlucky map the intersection next to an objective can be empty with no way to route around it.

detail: There is NO SEIZE ACTION, so a "Seize gate" chapter cannot be completed by the tool layer at all — independent of any bug. fe7_act's action enum is exactly ["wait","attack","staff","item"]. Chapter 1 Lyn HM's objective is "Seize gate" (read from the text buffer at 0x0202A5B4). Even given a perfect movement grid and a located gate tile, the best I could do is fe7_act(action:'wait') ON the gate, which ends the unit's turn standing on it and does not seize — seize is a separate entry on the unit's action menu, alongside Wait, that appears only when a lord stands on the gate/throne. So every Seize map in the game is currently unwinnable. This is compounded by the terrain gap already filed (I cannot locate the gate either), but the two are independent: fixing terrain lookup alone would let me find the gate and still not be able to take it. Worth noting the same likely applies to other menu-contextual actions I had no occasion to need this chapter — Visit (village), Door/Chest, Talk, Rescue/Drop, Trade — none are in the enum.
wanted: Add 'seize' to fe7_act's action enum: fe7_act(slot, x, y, action:'seize'), which walks the lord to the tile and picks the Seize entry, confirming by effect — the chapter-complete transition or the objective text changing — rather than by absence of error. It should fail with a specific message when the unit is not a lord or the tile is not the objective tile, per the fe7.ts convention that failures name the cause. More generally the action enum should cover the whole contextual action menu (seize, visit, door, chest, talk, rescue, drop, trade), since any of them being absent silently caps what a run can accomplish and, per the runbook, a missing action never errors — it just quietly never gets tried. Deriving the menu entries rather than scanning is the existing convention and applies here.

detail: Exact characterisation of the movement-grid stride bug, verified numerically — supersedes the guesswork in my earlier notes. fe7.ts reads the grid as base 0x030004AC + (y+2)*24 + x. The real buffer is at 0x03000478, stride 17, 14 rows = 238 bytes, ending at 0x03000566. Since 0x030004AC is 52 bytes into the real buffer, the render cell (x,y) actually shows real-buffer byte index 52 + (y+2)*24 + x. I verified this against a live fe7_reachable render: 216 of 240 cells matched the predicted byte EXACTLY. The other 24 were all at computed index >= 238, i.e. past the end of the grid buffer entirely — fe7.ts asks for 27*24 = 648 bytes from 0x030004AC (through 0x03000734) when only 238 bytes of grid exist. TWO CONSEQUENCES WORTH RECORDING. (1) Render rows y>=6 are read entirely from outside the buffer, and they were BYTE-IDENTICAL across all five fe7_reachable calls I made this chapter, from five different Lyn positions — that region of IWRAM is static, so those rows are constant garbage that never updates. A caller who trusted them would see a phantom movement range in the south-east of every map that never changes no matter where the unit stands. (2) Because the map is 15 wide but the stride is 17, columns 15 and 16 of each row are padding, and destination tiles whose alias lands on padding can NEVER validate. Concretely, this chapter: of the four tiles adjacent to the last brigand at (3,2), (4,2) aliases to true (16,6) = padding, never legal; (2,2) aliases to true (14,6), 16 tiles away from (2,2) for a Move-5 unit, unsatisfiable; (3,1) is impassable terrain anyway (so are (2,1) and (4,1) — a wall); and (3,3) aliases to true (5,8), which must be reachable SIMULTANEOUSLY with (3,3) though they are 7 apart, while every staging tile that would bridge them aliases to buffer row 13 (off-map, always FF) or outside the buffer. So the final enemy is unkillable and the chapter is unwinnable on the movement bug alone, on top of the missing seize action.
wanted: Same P0 fix as filed (walk the row-pointer table at 0x03000440 — 14 entries, stride 0x11, 0xFFFFFFFF terminator — and use pointer[y+2] per row, rather than hardcoding base/stride/rows). Adding here the two things that should be regression-tested once fixed, because both were silent: (a) assert that the tile holding cost 0 in the decoded grid equals the selected unit's position from its unit struct — that single check would have caught this immediately and cheaply, and belongs in fe7_reachable permanently; (b) assert the decoded range is CONNECTED, since the disconnected islands in the render were the visible tell that something was wrong. Also cap the read at the real buffer length instead of 648 bytes so out-of-buffer IWRAM can never be presented as movement cost.

detail: CORRECTION to my earlier note's proposed fix, plus direct proof that the movement grid is sized PER CHAPTER. Verified on THREE maps now. Lyn Ch.1 HM: pointer table at 0x03000440 holds 14 entries, stride 0x11 (17), data at 0x03000478, 238 bytes, terminated by 0xFFFFFFFF. Lyn Ch.7 HM "Siblings Abroad" (read live this session): 18 entries, stride 0x16 (22), data at 0x03000488, 396 bytes, terminated by 0x00000000. Ch.22 Hector per RAM.md: 27 entries, stride 0x18 (24), data at 0x030004AC, 648 bytes. All three satisfy the invariant "the table ends exactly where its own data begins" (0x440 + 4*count == first pointer, checks out at 14, 18 and 27), and stride runs 2 wider than the playable map width. Ch.7 decode verified end to end: reading 396 bytes from 0x03000488 at stride 22 with row = y+2 puts cost 0x00 at row 6 col 3 = (3,4), exactly matching Lyn's position from fe7_state. So the per-map sizing is now DIRECTLY OBSERVED, not inferred from RAM.md. THE CORRECTION: my earlier note said to walk the pointer table "until 0xFFFFFFFF". That is WRONG and would break on this very chapter — Ch.1 terminates the table with 0xFFFFFFFF but Ch.7 terminates it with 0x00000000, so a 0xFFFFFFFF-only sentinel check would run off the end of the table and treat garbage as row pointers. SEPARATELY, the failure MODE differs by map and is worse here than in Ch.1. On Ch.1 the misread produced 0xFF and REFUSED legal moves. On Ch.7 the over-read (fe7.ts asks 648 bytes from 0x030004AC; this map's grid is 396 bytes ending at 0x03000614) lands in ZEROED memory, and 0x00 decodes as "cost 0 = legal destination". fe7_reachable accordingly reported 319 tiles and 315 legal destinations against a true count of 39, drawing a solid block of cost-0 tiles from y=13 through y=24 — most of which are off the bottom of a 16-row map. So on this chapter the tool does not merely refuse good moves, it ACCEPTS roughly 300 destinations that do not exist.
wanted: Derive the geometry from the table, and do NOT rely on any sentinel value. The robust derivation, which holds on all three observed maps: rowCount = (read32(0x03000440) - 0x03000440) / 4  — i.e. the first pointer tells you where the table ends, and therefore how many entries it has; stride = read32(0x03000444) - read32(0x03000440); rowBase(y) = read32(0x03000440 + 4*(y+2)). Then read exactly rowCount*stride bytes and never one byte more, so zeroed or foreign memory can never be presented as cost 0. Checks: Ch.1 (0x478-0x440)/4 = 14, Ch.7 (0x488-0x440)/4 = 18, Ch.22 (0x4AC-0x440)/4 = 27. Add the assertion I proposed before — the tile holding cost 0 must equal the selected unit's position from its struct — since that single check catches every variant of this bug on every map. Also bound x by the real map width (stride - 2), because the last two columns of each row are padding and must never be offered as destinations.

detail: Throughout Ch.1 I repeatedly needed to know which tiles were threatened by enemies so I could stage units just outside their reach (especially cav #1, whose lance loses to axes, and Lyn, whose death ends the chapter). There is no tool for this, so every turn I hand-computed Manhattan distance (enemy move ~5 + 1 attack = radius 6) from each enemy to candidate destination tiles. That math is imprecise: it ignores terrain costs (forests cost 2, rivers/peaks are impassable), so my 'safe at Manhattan 7' tiles were only approximately safe, and I over-retreated cav #1 several times to be sure. It also cannot see ranged weapons. I got it right by being conservative, but it was the single most tedious and error-prone part of every turn.
wanted: fe7_threat() (or a flag on fe7_state / fe7_reachable) that returns the union of all enemies' actual attack ranges as a board overlay — computed from each enemy's real cost map plus weapon min/max range, the same way fe7_reachable already derives one unit's reachable set. Ideally annotate each tile with how many enemies threaten it and their max total damage, so 'is this staging tile safe, and if not how bad' is one call instead of manual Manhattan arithmetic that ignores terrain.

detail: When healing Lyn and cav #2 with a vulnerary via fe7_act(action:'item'), the tool doc says item_slot 'defaults to slot 0'. But slot 0 is almost always a weapon (Lyn's inventory was [sword, vulnerary, vulnerary]; cav #2's was [sword, lance, vulnerary]). So the default would try to 'use' a sword as a self-item. I knew to pass item_slot explicitly (1 for Lyn, 2 for cav #2), but a caller who trusts the default would either error or do something unintended, and the failure wouldn't obviously point at 'you picked a weapon'.
wanted: action:'item' should default item_slot to the first USABLE consumable in the inventory (scan for a healing/usable item, skipping weapons) rather than literal slot 0 — and if none exists, say so by name. At minimum, refuse a non-consumable slot with a message like 'slot 0 holds Iron Sword, not a usable item; unit carries a Vulnerary in slot 1'.

detail: Ch.2 (Seize throne, 15x10) has three House tiles at (0,7), (1,7) and (0,9) — fe7_terrain found them cleanly. There is no way to visit them: fe7_act has no 'visit' action, and 'wait' deliberately wraps UP to the menu's LAST entry, which is Wait. I probed the menu by calling fe7_act(slot 1, 1,7, action:'seize') on the house tile — that reported the action menu as [0x8b954a0, item, wait], i.e. Visit is entry index 0 and is the entry already highlighted when the menu opens. So a 'visit' action is a one-press addition on top of machinery that already exists (the seize path already reads each entry's ROM command pointer). Without it, three villages on this map are simply unreachable content, and I had to fall back on raw presses to test it.
wanted: fe7_act(slot, x, y, action: 'visit') — locate the entry by its ROM command pointer exactly as 'seize' does (pointer 0x08b954a0 appears to be Visit), press A, then hold A through the village dialogue until the map regains input, and report what was received (item added to inventory / gold / unit joined) by diffing the unit's inventory and the convoy. Also worth having fe7_terrain's 'find' results flag which houses are still unvisited, since terrain does not change after a visit.

detail: Ch.2's castle (x8-14, y0-7) is sealed: walls on every side and the only floor opening is the south aisle at (11,7), which is reachable from our start ONLY by crossing Mntn tiles at (6,8)/(6,9)/(7,7)/(7,8). fe7_reachable confirms cavaliers (cls28) cannot enter Mntn at all, so Sain and Kent are permanently cut off from the objective by the terrain. The house at (0,7) says outright "You might be able to create another entrance by hitting that section with...", and fe7_terrain shows exactly one anomalous wall tile — (8,3) is ID 0x1B while every other wall on the map is 0x1A. Probing the action menu from the adjacent tile (fe7_act slot 0, 7,3, action:'seize') returned [attack, item, wait] with no unit adjacent, which confirms the game will let you attack the wall. But fe7_act(action:'attack') refused: "no enemy is within its weapon range 1-1 of (7,3)" — it validates against the enemy unit array, and a destructible wall is not a unit. So the map's intended second entrance cannot be opened with the tools as they stand. Worse, the refusal was not a refusal: it had already moved Lyn to (7,3) and it "Waited instead", spending her turn on an action I did not ask for.
wanted: Two things. (1) fe7_act(slot, x, y, action: 'attack', target_terrain: {x, y}) — or simply let action:'attack' fall through to the menu's Attack entry and the game's own default target when no enemy unit is adjacent, since the menu-reading machinery from 'seize' can already confirm an Attack entry exists. Destructible objects (walls, snags) live in their own table, not the enemy array, so the range check needs to consult that too; fe7_terrain could flag ID 0x1B as destructible and report its HP. (2) Separately: fe7_act must never substitute a different action when the requested one is unavailable. Silently committing Wait costs the unit its turn and puts it on a tile I only chose for the attack. It should cancel with B and leave the unit unspent, exactly as the destination-unreachable path already does.

detail: Rescue and Trade both showed up as real entries on Kent's action menu at (0,7) with Sain adjacent at (1,7) — the menu was [Visit, Rescue, Trade, Item, Wait] — and neither has a tool action. Trade matters immediately on this map: Sain carries only an Iron Lance and no vulnerary, and sat at 14/19 all chapter while Kent stood next to him at (1,7)/(0,7) holding two vulneraries. Rescue matters because Lyn (Move 5, foot) is the only unit that can cross the Mntn barrier, and a cavalier who could carry her would change the whole route. Menu index is not stable — the same house tile gave a 3-entry menu [Visit, Item, Wait] for Sain with nobody adjacent and a 5-entry menu for Kent with Sain adjacent — so these have to be located by ROM command pointer the way 'seize' does, never by a fixed index.
wanted: fe7_act(slot, x, y, action: 'trade', target_slot, give_item_slot?, take_item_slot?) and action: 'rescue' / 'drop' / 'take' with target_slot and, for drop, a destination tile. Trade does not consume the action in FE7, so it probably wants to be its own tool (fe7_trade) that leaves the unit selected and unspent; a tool that ends the unit's turn would make it nearly useless. Both should report the resulting inventories / the rescued unit's state read back from memory rather than assuming the press landed.

detail: The destructible wall at (8,3) has 30 HP and takes 15 from Kent's Iron Lance, so it needs exactly two rounds — but nothing in the tool layer told me any of that. fe7_terrain reports the tile as ID 0x1B named "Wall", identical in the legend to the 27 indestructible 0x1A walls, with no HP and no destructible flag; fe7_inspect returns the string "Wall" for both (8,2) 0x1A and (8,3) 0x1B, so the readout cannot distinguish them either. The only place the 30 HP and the Mt 15 / Hit 100 appeared was the target-select screen, which I had to reach with raw presses and read off a screenshot — exactly what the runbook says never to do. I also had no forecast: fe7_forecast takes an enemy target_slot, and the wall has none, so I could not compare Iron Sword (Mt 13, three rounds) against Iron Lance (Mt 15, two rounds) without opening the real weapon menu and reading the numbers on screen. Choosing the lance saved a whole turn.
wanted: fe7_terrain should mark destructible tiles and print their current HP — the game clearly tracks it, since the tile stays 0x1B at 15/30 and presumably flips to a floor/plain ID at 0. And fe7_forecast should accept a terrain target the same way I want fe7_act to (fe7_forecast(slot, x, y, target_terrain: {x,y})), reporting Mt and hit per weapon in the unit's inventory so the weapon choice is a read, not a screenshot. Related: neither fe7_act nor fe7_forecast lets me pick WHICH weapon to fight with — the game opened a weapon-select menu (Iron sword / Iron lance) that the tools always resolve by taking the default, and here the default was the wrong choice.

detail: fe7_act(slot 1, 11,2, action:'attack', target_slot 0) against the boss returned a failure — "Attack was chosen, but the unit never became spent within 20s. Enemy HP: #0 20->20. Something is still on screen." — when in fact nothing had gone wrong. The boss (Glass) has a pre-battle conversation that fires between confirming the attack and the combat resolving, and the 20s spent-flag wait expired while the dialogue was still up. fe7_unstick showed the text buffer holding "....Who do you think you are?...What chance do you think.you hav", so the diagnosis was easy, but the report itself was actively misleading: "Enemy HP 20->20" reads as "the attack did not land", and the runbook's rule is to not repeat a failed call — re-issuing this one would have re-attacked with a unit whose first attack was still mid-resolution. Four A presses cleared the quote and the combat then resolved normally (Sain killed the boss). Every boss in the game has one of these, so this will recur on every chapter's decisive attack — the single attack where a bogus failure is most expensive.
wanted: fe7_act's post-commit wait should press A on a cadence while it polls, exactly as fe7_wait already does, instead of only polling — a battle conversation, a level-up and a weapon-broke message are all cleared by the same press. Failing that, it should distinguish "spent flag never set AND no dialogue on screen" (a real dropped input) from "spent flag not set yet, text buffer non-empty" (an event is playing) and say so, rather than reporting stale before/after HP that implies the attack missed.

detail: fe7_act's seize probe is the only tool that can enumerate an action menu, and I ended up using it three times purely as a reconnaissance call (on the house at (1,7), on the tile beside the breakable wall at (7,3), and on the throne at (11,1) with a non-lord). It works, but it only names the commands it already knows — the reports came back as [0x8b954a0, item, wait], [attack, item, wait] and [0x8b9559c, item, trade, wait]. I had to cross-reference a screenshot to learn that 0x8b954a0 is Visit, and I still do not know whether 0x8b9559c is Rescue (the on-screen entry order at (7,3) and (0,7) suggests it is) or something else. When the answer to "can this unit do X here" is a bare ROM address, the probe cannot answer the question it is best at. Also note the failure sentence conflates two causes it can actually tell apart: "Either this tile is not the objective, or this unit is not a lord" — the tool knows the unit's class and could say which.
wanted: A first-class fe7_menu(slot, x, y) that moves the unit, reads every entry, names each one from a command-pointer table (Attack, Staff, Visit, Seize, Rescue, Drop, Take, Trade, Item, Talk, Door, Chest, Wait), and backs out pressing nothing — i.e. the seize probe promoted to its own tool, since that is what I kept using it as. Unknown pointers should still print as hex so the table can be filled in from run logs. And the seize failure should name the actual cause: it knows whether the class is a lord and whether the tile is the objective.

detail: Nothing in the tool layer reports the chapter objective, the turn limit, or the win/loss conditions. I only learned this map was "Seize throne" because fe7_unstick happened to return a screenshot with the objective banner on it, and the runbook explicitly warns that a Gate or Throne tile does NOT imply a Seize objective (Lyn Ch.7 is Defeat-Boss with a gate). So on this chapter the single most important planning fact came from pixels. Related: I could not tell whether there was a turn limit, which is exactly the input needed to decide between "spend three turns walking Kent to the last brigand at (13,8) for XP" and "seize now". I guessed.
wanted: fe7_state should carry an objective line — objective type and text, the target tile if it is Seize, the turn limit if one exists, and the protect-target if the chapter has one. The strings are on screen so the game has them in RAM; RAM.md would want the addresses. It is one line and it changes how every turn is planned.

detail: fe7_reachable(slot 1) on Sain, who had already acted this turn (he used a vulnerary at (11,2)), returned "Pressed A on (11,2) but unit #1 never became selected — input swallowed." That diagnosis is false. Nothing was swallowed: the game correctly refuses to select a spent unit, and fe7_state had already reported him ACTED. "Input swallowed" is the one phrase that points at the emulator bridge rather than at the game, so it invites exactly the wrong response — retrying, or reaching for fe7_unstick and raw presses — for a condition that is a plain, permanent refusal until next turn. fe7_act already guards this ("refuses to act unless the unit is deployed, alive and unspent"); fe7_reachable does not, even though it is the cheaper call and therefore the one you reach for first when scouting.
wanted: fe7_reachable should read the has-acted flag before pressing anything and fail with "unit #1 has already acted this turn" — the same pre-flight guard fe7_act uses. More generally, "input swallowed" should be reserved for cases where a precondition check passed and the press still did not land; every state the tool could have checked in advance deserves its own message.

detail: Follow-up to the fe7_reachable-on-a-spent-unit finding, and the more serious half of it: the tool did not just misdiagnose, it left the game in a changed state and did not say so. Pressing A on a spent unit is not a no-op — the game treats the tile as empty and OPENS THE FIELD MENU (Unit / Status / Options / Suspend / End). fe7_reachable returned "input swallowed" and did not press B, so the field menu stayed open. The very next call, fe7_act(slot 2, 10,2, 'wait'), then failed with "Could not drive the cursor onto unit #2 at (10,2). Input appears blocked (event/animation)" — a second wrong diagnosis caused by the first tool's leftover state. Only fe7_unstick found it: "MENU OPEN at 0x202583D — 5 entries". This is the field menu whose fourth entry is Suspend and fifth is End; a stray A or a wrapping Up here ends the player phase or suspends the chapter. fe7_reachable's own docs say it presses B afterwards unless keep_selected is set, but that cleanup evidently does not run on the failure path.
wanted: Every fe7_* tool that presses A must press B on its failure path too, not only on its success path — and should verify it is back to a free cursor (the fe7_unstick probe already knows how) before returning. Any tool that returns having left a menu open should say which menu and at what address, so the next call is not flying blind. Combined with the pre-flight has-acted guard, the A here would never have been pressed at all.

detail: Seizing worked first try — fe7_act(slot 0, 11,1, 'seize') reported "Menu was [seize, item, trade, wait], Seize at index 0" — but the chapter-ending cutscene that follows is not driveable by any tool. fe7_wait is the tool for "press A until things resolve", and it returned "Already the player phase (turn 10)" without pressing anything, because the phase byte stays 0x00 all the way through the ending scene, the Mani Katti scene, the world-map narration and the Chapter 3 opening. So the only way through roughly 160 presses of dialogue was raw mgba_press_sequence blocks with a screenshot between each to see whether it was over — which is exactly the pixel-reading and raw-press loop the tool layer exists to eliminate, and it is the last thing that happens in every single chapter.
wanted: fe7_advance_events(timeout_ms) — press A on a cadence while the text buffer is non-empty or the map is not accepting free-cursor input, stopping when fe7_unstick's probe reports FREE CURSOR, and return what it landed on (same map / new chapter, turn, unit count). Alternatively give fe7_wait a mode that keys off "is the map accepting input" rather than off the phase byte, since the phase byte is 0x00 during a cutscene and is therefore the wrong signal. Either way it should report the chapter transition — I only knew Chapter 3 had loaded because fe7_state suddenly showed turn 1, three full-HP units on new tiles and a green NPC.

detail: Ch3 has villages at (2,2) and (3,6). I moved Kent (slot 2) onto the village at (3,6) intending to visit it. fe7_act only supports wait/attack/staff/item/seize, so it wrapped the action menu up to 'Wait' and committed that — which does NOT trigger the village. When a unit ends movement on a village tile, the action menu contains a 'Visit' entry; selecting Wait skips the village entirely and wastes the visit. Kent is now parked on (3,6) spent, and the village is still unvisited (screenshot readout still says 'Village', house graphic intact). With the current tools, villages are effectively unvisitable, so their items/recruits/gold are unreachable.
wanted: fe7_act(slot, x, y, action: 'visit') that locates the 'Visit' menu entry by reading each entry's ROM command pointer (the same technique fe7_act already uses for 'seize'), presses A on it, and then presses A through the resulting village dialogue, confirming by effect (item added to inventory, or the village terrain/graphic changing to 'visited'). Should report what the village gave.

detail: Attacking the boss Migal (enemy #0) with fe7_act(action='attack') stalled both times: the tool moved the unit, chose Attack, then reported 'the unit never became spent within 20s. Something is still on screen' with enemy HP unchanged. The cause was a boss battle quote — Migal has a PRE-battle quote when first engaged (Sain's attack) and a DEATH quote when killed (Kent's attack). These dialogue boxes appear after Attack is confirmed but before/around the battle resolves, and fe7_act does not press A through them, so it times out. The battle actually DID resolve underneath (Sain's brought Migal 25->3 and Sain took the counter; Kent's killed him). I had to clear the quotes manually with mgba_press_buttons A — and over-pressing A past the quote/EXP opened the field menu then the Character status screen, which then needed B to exit. fe7_unstick correctly diagnosed each stage (dialogue 'INPUT SWALLOWED' vs the status menu vs free cursor).
wanted: fe7_act should detect a post-confirm dialogue box (boss battle/death quote, and likely other event text) the same way fe7_wait does, and press A to clear it — then confirm the unit became spent — instead of timing out. Ideally it should stop pressing A the instant the spent flag sets / cursor frees, so it never overshoots into the field menu and status screen.

detail: fe7_forecast left the game in a stuck, unrecoverable-by-B state. Chapter 3, turn 7, one enemy left (#5 brigand, 5 HP, at (3,7)). I tried to forecast Wil (#3 archer) attacking #5: first from (3,9) it returned 'moved to (3,9) but no menu entry led to a forecast (menu count 4; tried 0=no-forecast). Most likely nothing is in range' — but (3,9) IS range 2 from (3,7). Then from (5,7) it returned 'reached (5,7) but the action menu could not be located. Nothing changed.' After that, the game was left with a unit SELECTED in move-select mode (blue move-range renders and tracks the cursor; text buffer shows 'Wait'; fe7_unstick reports 'selected unit: #0 cls02 at (3,9)' and 'FREE CURSOR'). Crucially, pressing B ~10 times across several calls did NOT deselect it, and fe7_act on a different unit (#4) fails with 'Selection failed: pressed A but +0x0C bit 0 never set' because a unit is already selected. So a forecast that failed to locate the menu did NOT unwind — it left the unit selected/moved and the UI wedged, and normal B-cancel does not clear it.
wanted: fe7_forecast must guarantee it unwinds on EVERY exit path — including when the action menu can't be located or no target is in range — by pressing B enough to return to a clean free-cursor state and verifying the 'selected unit' pointer is cleared before returning. When it can't parse the menu it should back all the way out, not leave the unit selected/moved. Separately, fe7_unstick could offer a 'force-clear selection' recovery that reliably returns to free cursor, since plain B presses did not.

detail: Planning turn 1 of a Protect/defend chapter (15x14, green NPC at (7,3), 14 enemies), the single most important question was 'which tiles can enemies reach and attack next enemy phase'. There is no tool for that. fe7_reachable only works on a PLAYER slot, so to find the chokepoints I had to read fe7_terrain, hand-decode which terrain IDs were impassable (Wall 1A, Brace 3F), cross-check that against a cavalier's cost grid, and then manually compute Manhattan distances from all 14 enemy positions to candidate blocking tiles to see who could reach what. That is ~15 minutes of arithmetic that the game itself already computes.
wanted: fe7_threat({ faction: 'enemy', slots?: [..] }) returning the union of enemy move+attack ranges as an ASCII overlay (the game's own red 'danger zone' toggle), ideally annotated per tile with which enemy slots threaten it and at what range. Minimum viable: fe7_reachable(slot, faction: 'enemy') so at least one enemy's move range can be read from the game instead of estimated.

detail: fe7_forecast for Wil (#4, Iron Bow, range 2) at (6,7) vs brigand #3 at (6,9) returned a defender block of 'dmg 0 x44 (ATK 3 - DEF 5) hit 255% crit 255% AS 5 avo 10 ddg 0'. The brigand physically cannot counterattack a bow at range 2, so there is no defender side to this fight at all. The numbers are not merely zero, they are junk: 255% is 0xFF (uninitialised), and 'x44' is exactly the number of uses left on Wil's own Iron Bow (2Cx44) from fe7_state, so the blow-count field is reading a stale/unrelated byte. Compare the melee forecast I ran one call earlier (Florina vs the boss), whose defender block was correct — so the bug is specific to the no-counter case. In-game the forecast panel just shows '--' for the defender here. I could tell it was nonsense this time, but on a fight where I am deciding whether a wounded unit survives, a plausible-looking fabricated defender block is exactly the kind of thing that gets a unit killed.
wanted: fe7_forecast should detect that the defender has no weapon that reaches the attacking range and print 'defender: no counterattack (out of range)' instead of decoding the struct. More generally it should sanity-gate the struct before formatting: hit/crit of 0xFF and a blow count above ~4 are impossible, and should be reported as 'forecast struct not populated' rather than rendered as numbers.

detail: fe7_state reports inventories as raw hex pairs — Lyn '[01x28,6Bx3,0Ax45]', Wil '[2Cx44]', boss '[28x20]'. Nothing names the item or gives its range, might or uses, so every planning decision needed me to guess from context: I inferred 0x2C was a bow only because Wil's class could not counter at range 1, and 0x1F/0x20 were axes only because the units holding them were brigands. The 'x44'/'x28' suffix is uses remaining, which reads like a quantity and misled me once already (see the forecast note, where a blow count of 'x44' coincided with Wil's bow uses). Concretely this cost me: I could not tell whether the boss's 0x28 was a Steel Axe (range 1, safe to stand next to at range 2) or a Hand Axe (range 1-2, which would have made Wil's whole firing position unsafe), so I had to plan around the worse case with no way to check.
wanted: fe7_state should render items as 'Iron Sword (28)' with a name from an item table, and annotate weapons with range and might, e.g. 'Iron Bow rng2 mt6 (44 uses)'. Range is the field that actually changes decisions — a per-unit 'threat range 1' / '1-2' / '2' summary line would be enough on its own. The item name table is a static ROM lookup, not per-chapter, so it does not conflict with the never-hardcode-what-the-game-computes rule.

detail: Turn 5. Cavalier #1 was at 9/20 holding the south doorway at (6,9) and had spent his last vulnerary on turn 2, so he had no way to heal. Lyn (#0, (7,5)) is carrying 6Bx3 and Florina (#3) 6Bx2 — two full vulneraries sitting unused. Cavalier #1 has Move 7 and could reach (7,6), adjacent to Lyn, this turn, so the handover is legal in game terms and costs nothing but a trade. There is no trade action, so instead I had to pull him off the front line entirely to (6,7) and backfill the doorway with Wil, who cannot counterattack at melee range — I gave up the counter-kills on that tile for the rest of the chapter purely because 10 HP could not move one tile sideways. This is the second-order cost that makes it worth more than it looks: the missing trade did not just cost HP, it forced a worse unit into the chokepoint.
wanted: A standalone tool, since trading does not consume the unit's action in FE7: fe7_trade({ slot, target_slot, give?: [item_slot], take?: [item_slot] }) — move-then-trade is also needed, so either accept x/y like fe7_act does, or add action:'trade' with target_slot + item_slot to fe7_act and have it report that the unit is still unspent afterwards. Also needed for the common case of handing a fresh weapon to a unit whose iron sword is about to break.

detail: The boss (#13, cls12, 30 HP) has been orthogonally adjacent to Florina at (11,5)/(12,5) since enemy phase 1 and has dealt her zero damage across five consecutive enemy phases. fe7_forecast says it hits her for 11 at 65%, so five straight misses is 0.35^5 = 0.5% — this is not luck, the boss simply does not initiate. It DOES counter: the only damage Florina took all chapter (17->6) was the counterattack when she attacked it on turn 3. It also moved exactly once, (13,7)->(12,5) on EP1, then never again. This mattered a lot and I could only learn it by spending a unit's HP to test: because the boss parks on (12,5), which is the ONLY tile orthogonally adjacent to the east chokepoint (11,5), the boss's own body seals the east door against its four allies queued at (12,3),(12,4),(13,5),(12,6). Had I known its AI on turn 1 I would have pulled Florina out entirely and had a fifth unit free for six turns.
wanted: fe7_state should report each enemy's AI disposition, which lives in the unit struct (FE7 has AI bytes at unit+0x38..0x3B, plus the 'immobile' status bit). Even a coarse tag per enemy would change play completely: 'stationary/counter-only', 'guards until approached', 'charges'. Sketch: fe7_state adding '#13 cls12 (12,5) 30/30 ai=counter-only,immobile' — or a dedicated fe7_ai() dumping the raw AI bytes with a decode, so the values can be catalogued into RAM.md across chapters.

detail: Two failures in one call, at the end-of-chapter victory event on turn 8. (1) fe7_unstick's VERDICT read 'POSSIBLY an attack target selection (cursor frozen, no menu index found, forecast populated)' and recommended 'If it IS target select, B backs out and A would COMMIT the attack.' It was not target select at all — its own text buffer in the same output read \".....The enemy's fled......... !..We've won!!!.\", i.e. the chapter had been won and the game was playing the victory event. Acting on the verdict would have had me pressing B to 'back out' of a cutscene. The stale-forecast gate is documented as unreliable and it duly produced a confident wrong verdict, while the one field that WAS decisive — the text buffer — did not feed into the verdict at all. (2) The recommendation says 'Confirm with the screenshot before acting', but the screenshot was a completely black frame (mid-fade), so the prescribed confirmation step was impossible. Separately: I could never determine the win condition from any tool. I read 'Protect / 1 / 7 Turn' off the turn-1 screenshot and concluded it was a 7-turn defend, so I played a pure turtle and expected the chapter to end after enemy phase 7. It did not; it ended on turn 8 when the enemies routed/fled. I planned six turns around a guess made from pixels, which is exactly what the runbook says not to do — but there is no alternative.
wanted: Three things. (a) fe7_unstick should weight the text buffer in its verdict, and recognise victory/defeat strings — a verdict of 'CHAPTER EVENT: text buffer reads \"...We've won...\" — press A to advance' would have been unambiguous. It should also say when the screenshot is a blank/black frame rather than telling me to read it. (b) The 'forecast pair populated' signal is documented as stale-prone and should be demoted: do not let it alone produce a 'target selection' verdict. (c) A fe7_objective() tool reading the chapter's objective type and its parameter out of memory — 'Defeat all enemies', 'Seize (x,y)', 'Survive N turns', 'Protect <unit>' — plus the turn limit if any. This is the single most important fact in a chapter and it is currently only obtainable by squinting at a screenshot.

detail: At the start of Chapter 5, I had no way to read the chapter's win condition (objective) from the tool layer. fe7_state gives turn/phase/units and fe7_terrain gives the map, but neither reports whether the objective is Rout / Seize / Defeat-boss / Defend / Escape, nor any turn limit or protect-target. The RUNBOOK explicitly says 'Read the objective; do not infer it from terrain' — but there is no tool that does that, so I am forced to infer from context (bandits attacking = presumably Rout).
wanted: fe7_objective — reads the chapter objective struct and returns e.g. {type:'rout'|'seize'|'defeat_boss'|'defend'|'escape', target_slot?, turn_limit?, protect_slot?}. Even just the objective-type byte and any turn limit would let me plan instead of guess.

detail: Turn 5 Lyn (slot0) attacked enemy #4 (cls18, inventory only [2Cx?], a staff) from (12,1); fe7_act reported Lyn 'Self: HP 17/17' and the forecast showed the defender dealing 'dmg 0 x44'. After the enemy phase Lyn was at 11/17 — she lost 6 HP. The only enemy near her was #4, which had MOVED AWAY to (13,2) and whose staff (2C) use-count dropped by 1; the boss was in the far SE corner (14,9), unreachable. I could not tell what dealt Lyn 6 damage, nor what enemy #4's staff did (it did not heal itself — it stayed at 8/20). A cls18 enemy holding only a staff should not be able to deal melee damage, so either #4 has an offensive staff/second weapon the state view doesn't surface, or the damage came from a source fe7_state/fe7_wait don't report.
wanted: fe7_wait (or a post-enemy-phase report) should attribute HP changes: e.g. 'Lyn -6 from enemy #4 (Lightning staff / etc.)'. And fe7_state should show a unit's full weapon capability, flagging offensive staves, so I can anticipate ranged staff damage rather than being surprised by it.

detail: fe7_act(slot=4, action='staff', target_slot=1) failed with 'Unit #4 carries no staff (inventory: 2C)'. Unit #4 is class cls18 (the same class as the enemy 'clerics' on this map) and item 0x2C is its ONLY item — almost certainly its Heal staff. The tool's staff-detection does not include item id 0x2C, so my only dedicated healer cannot heal at all through the tool layer. This left cav #1 stuck at 7/20 next to the boss with no way to top it up before the enemy phase. Note: enemy #4 earlier decremented this same 0x2C item's use-count during the enemy phase, consistent with it being a functional (heal or offensive) staff in-engine.
wanted: fe7_act action='staff' should recognize item id 0x2C (and any other staff ids missing from the list) as a staff, by reading the item's weapon-type/rank from the item table rather than matching a hardcoded id set. At minimum, fall back to 'the unit's class can wield staves and this item's type is staff' so new staff ids are handled without a code change.

detail: cav #2 (cls28 cavalier) is a sword+lance user carrying an iron lance (0x14, slot 0) and two iron swords (0x01) it picked up as loot. Against the AXE boss it should use the LANCE for weapon-triangle advantage (+1 dmg, +~15 hit), but the forecast/attack used a SWORD (ATK 15, hit 75%, and swords are at a DISADVANTAGE vs axes), doing 7x2. Picking up the dropped sword appears to have left a sword equipped. There is no fe7_act option to change a unit's equipped weapon, so I can't force the lance and am stuck attacking the axe boss at weapon-triangle disadvantage.
wanted: An equip capability: e.g. fe7_act(slot, action='equip', item_slot) or an `equip_slot` parameter on the attack action so I can pick the weapon before committing (and fe7_forecast should let me forecast per-weapon to compare). Even a standalone fe7_equip(slot, item_slot) would do.

detail: Chapter 22 starts on the Preparations menu (phase byte 0x40, "green/prep"). Every fe7_* action tool refuses in this phase (fe7_act/fe7_inspect require phase 0x00), and fe7_unstick's only advice is "call fe7_wait", which is wrong here — prep does not end on its own, it needs START/Fight!. There is no tool to read or change the deployment list, swap items between units, visit the armoury/shop, or press Fight!. I had to fall back to raw mgba_press_buttons to leave the menu, which is exactly what the runbook says not to do.
wanted: fe7_prep({action:'list'}) returning the deployable roster with deployed/benched flags, fe7_prep({action:'deploy'|'bench', roster_slot}), fe7_prep({action:'trade', from, to, item_slot}), and fe7_prep({action:'fight'}) that presses START and confirms, verified by the phase byte flipping to 0x00. Also: fe7_unstick should recognise phase 0x40 with the "Select which units to field" text and say "press START", not "call fe7_wait".

detail: Turn 2, Ch.22. I am setting a wall at (10,3)/(11,3) and need to know which tiles the 36 enemies can actually reach next enemy phase — the whole decision (how far forward to stand, whether the healer at (12,2) is safe, whether a sortie can retreat out of range) is a threat-range question. fe7_reachable only accepts a PLAYER slot, so there is no way to get an enemy's movement range at all, let alone the union of 36 of them. I ended up eyeballing Manhattan distance off fe7_state coordinates, which is exactly what fe7_reachable's own docs warn against ("terrain cost is visible in the grid, so don't assume Manhattan"). I also cannot see which enemies have already acted this phase.
wanted: fe7_threat({faction:'enemy', slots?:[...], include_weapon_range:true}) returning a board-sized ASCII overlay of tiles reachable-and-attackable by any (or a named) enemy, ideally with per-tile attacker count. Also fe7_reachable({slot, faction:'enemy'|'green'}) for a single unit. Note the game populates the cost grid only for the SELECTED unit, so this likely needs the same trick the AI uses or an offline flood-fill over the terrain-cost layer + the occupancy layer, both of which are already decoded.

detail: fe7_state lists green NPCs as bare "g46 cls14 Lv7 (10,7) HP11/21" — no stats, no inventory — while players and enemies get the full line. On Ch.22 that matters twice over: the objective unit itself is a green (g41 cls49 Lv1 (10,1) HP10/10, i.e. Nils), so "how much damage does Nils survive" and "can he be healed / does he carry a vulnerary" are unanswerable, and the green array turned over between turn 1 and turn 2 (two knights died, three new greens appeared at (16,1),(17,3),(18,3)) with no indication that the slot indices had been reused — I only caught it by diffing classes by hand. fe7_act's staff action already accepts target_faction:'green', so healing a green is supported while reading one is not.
wanted: Give greens the same line format as players/enemies (stats + items), and flag the objective/must-protect unit explicitly. Also mark newly-arrived and departed units between calls, or expose a stable unit id (character pointer) alongside the slot index, since green slots are recycled.

detail: Turn 3. #5 (cls12, inventory [1F Iron Axe x17, 28 Hand Axe x5, 28 Hand Axe x20]) at (10,3), enemy #21 (archer) at (10,5), distance 2. fe7_forecast(slot 5, 10,3, target 21) SUCCEEDED and returned a full forecast — ATK 23 = Str 16 + Hand Axe Mt 7, i.e. it silently switched to the Hand Axe (1-2) to produce the numbers. I then issued the identical fe7_act(slot 5, 10,3, action 'attack', target_slot 21) and got: "Unit #5 moved to (10,3) but Attack is unavailable — no enemy is within its weapon range 1-1 of (10,3)." Two tools, same unit, same tile, same target, opposite answers — and the forecast is the one that lied, because it reported an attack I could not actually make. Worse, fe7_act then "Waited instead", spending the unit's whole turn on a failed action, which directly contradicts its own docs ("Cancels cleanly with B on any pre-commit failure, leaving the unit unspent"). On a wall unit in a chokepoint that was survivable; on a unit I needed to reposition it would have cost the chapter.</detail>
wanted: (1) fe7_act must NEVER fall back to Wait — on a refused attack it should press B and return unspent, exactly as documented. (2) fe7_forecast must forecast with the weapon that would ACTUALLY be used, or state plainly which weapon it equipped and that equipping is a separate step. (3) The underlying gap: there is no way to equip/choose a weapon. Add fe7_act({slot, x, y, action:'equip', item_slot}) or a `weapon_slot` parameter on 'attack' that selects the weapon from the attack menu before choosing a target, so a 1-2 weapon can be used at range 2 while a 1-range weapon is equipped.

detail: Turn 4. Lucius (#4, cls1E Monk, inventory [3E Lightning (type 6 light), 4A Heal (type 4 staff) x7]) moved to (11,2) next to Hector at 23/30 and I called fe7_act(action:'staff', target_slot:0). Result: "Index 0 did not lead to staff target select (menu count 6, attack no, trade yes -> index 0) — the staff proc signature was not found. Backed out; unit #4 unspent at (12,1)." Two problems. (a) The message describes the tool's own internals — menu count, a derived index, a missing "staff proc signature" — and never states the actual cause, which is almost certainly that a Monk has staff rank 0 and therefore has no Staff command at all. RUNBOOK.md warns about exactly this case, and RAM.md records "Lucius carried 0x3E (type 6) and 0x4A (type 4), and his staff list had count 1", which reads as evidence he CAN use it — the type-4 inventory filter is not a usability test, and nothing in the tools distinguishes the two. I spent a unit's turn and a planning cycle finding out. (b) The same line reports "trade yes" — the game's menu offers Trade — while fe7_act has no trade action, so the tool can see a command it cannot issue. Credit where due: this path DID back out cleanly and leave the unit unspent, unlike the attack path on turn 3.
wanted: Check the unit's weapon-rank array for the staff type BEFORE walking it anywhere, and fail with "unit #4 cls1E has staff rank 0 — this class cannot use staves; its 4A Heal is dead weight" without moving or spending it. More generally, fe7_state should show each unit's usable weapon types (or mark unusable inventory items with a flag), since "carries a staff" and "can use a staff" are different facts and only the second one matters. And add the Trade action the menu is already offering.

detail: ROOT CAUSE of the turn-3 failure, confirmed and located. Lucius (#4) with Lightning (0x3E, range byte 0x12 = min 1, max 2) EQUIPPED in slot 0 moved to (10,2) and was told: "Attack is unavailable — no enemy is within its weapon range 2-1 of (10,2)." The printed range is 2-1: min greater than max, an empty interval, so no tile can ever satisfy it. src/fe7.ts:609 reads `{ min: b[0] & 0x0f, max: (b[0] >> 4) & 0x0f }` and the comment at src/fe7.ts:52 says "range (hi nibble max, lo min)" — both are backwards. RAM.md is explicit and Confirmed the other way ("+0x19 range, packed — high nibble = min, low nibble = max", settled by the ballista entries 0x34-0x36 reading 0x3A = 3-10), and my own ROM dump of the item table agrees. CONSEQUENCE: fe7_act cannot perform ANY attack at range 2 with a 1-2 weapon — every hand axe, javelin, short spear, light/anima/dark tome decodes to the empty range 2-1. Symmetric weapons (0x11 sword/axe 1-1, 0x22 bow 2-2) are unaffected, which is why this survived until now, and it also explains turn 3: #5's Iron Axe printed "1-1" correctly while both its Hand Axes silently decoded to the empty 2-1, so the union looked like 1-1. fe7_forecast does NOT share the bug — it happily produced a Hand Axe forecast at range 2 — which is why the two tools contradicted each other. Second occurrence of the Wait-fallback: this failure ALSO spent Lucius ("Waited instead") at (10,2). Not fixing mid-run per CLAUDE.md; playing the rest of the chapter melee-only.
wanted: src/fe7.ts:609 -> `{ min: (b[0] >> 4) & 0x0f, max: b[0] & 0x0f }`, and fix the comment at src/fe7.ts:52. Then add a regression check: Hand Axe 0x28 must decode 1-2, Iron Sword 0x01 1-1, Iron Bow 0x2D 2-2, Ballista 0x34 3-10 (the asymmetric one is the whole test). Worth auditing every other consumer of itemRange() for the same assumption, and worth adding the cheap invariant min <= max with a loud throw, since an inverted range fails as "nothing in range" rather than as an error.

detail: Two smaller things from turn 4, both cross-tool consistency. (1) GREEN SLOT NUMBERING DISAGREES BETWEEN TOOLS. fe7_state lists the green array as "g41 cls49 Lv1 (10,1) HP10/10 ... g48"; fe7_act, refusing a move onto that same tile, calls it "OCCUPIED by a green unit (slot #0, cls49, HP 10/10)". Same unit, two names: g41 and #0. fe7_act's staff action takes target_slot together with target_faction:'green', and nothing says which numbering that parameter expects — so healing Nils, the one unit this chapter is about, is a coin flip between 0 and 41, and target_slot is documented as verified-before-committing, which means a wrong guess costs a turn rather than erroring usefully. (Credit: the refusal message itself is otherwise excellent — it names faction, slot, class and HP, exactly as CLAUDE.md asks.) (2) fe7_act's staff success line reported "+0x0C=0x02", which reads as not-yet-spent; the Wait path reports 0x42. I burned a call issuing a second action to find out, and got "Unit #10 has already acted this phase (+0x0C = 0x42)" — so the flag had simply not settled when the staff line was printed.
wanted: Use one label for greens everywhere — either g41.. or 0.. — and say explicitly in fe7_act's target_slot doc which one target_faction:'green' indexes. Best: let fe7_act accept the exact string fe7_state printed ("g41"). For (2): re-read +0x0C after a short settle, as the Wait path evidently does, and print a plain "unit is now spent" / "still unspent" rather than the raw flag.

detail: Turn 5. fe7_act(slot 9, 10,3, 'attack', target_slot 35) returned: "Unit #9 moved to (10,3) and Attack was chosen, but the unit never became spent within 20s. Enemy HP: #35 23->23. Something is still on screen." That reads as a failed attack that did no damage. It was not — the attack had ALREADY KILLED #35; what was on screen was the boss/enemy death quote ("..6..I fought with honor....I can ask nothing more....."), which stalls the has-acted flag and made the HP re-read return the pre-combat value. fe7_wait presses A once a second precisely to clear death quotes and reinforcement text; fe7_act does not, even though committing an attack is the single most likely way to trigger one. Because the report looked like a failure I had to fe7_unstick, then drive raw mgba_press_buttons A and B by hand, and my A landed on empty ground and opened the FIELD menu (Unit/Status/Options/Suspend/End) with Suspend one press away — the exact situation the runbook says never to get into. fe7_state afterwards confirmed #35 gone, enemies 50->49, #9 spent at (10,3) on 37/37. Reporting a completed kill as "nothing happened" is the worst shape of failure available: it invites re-issuing an action that already landed.
wanted: fe7_act should poll-and-press-A the way fe7_wait does while waiting for the has-acted flag — a death quote, a level-up, a weapon-broke message and a battle-result box are all normal outcomes of a committed attack, not anomalies. It should also re-read target HP AFTER the flag settles, not before. And when it does give up, it must distinguish "the action never committed" from "the action committed and I could not confirm it", because those demand opposite responses from the caller.

detail: Turn 6. Player #6 (Iron Lance, range 1-1) attacked enemy #6, an archer with an Iron Bow (range 2-2), from (11,3) onto (11,4) — range 1, so the archer physically cannot counter. fe7_act's embedded forecast block printed: "defender: dmg 0 x30 (ATK 8 - DEF 8) hit 255% crit 255% AS 8 avo 16 ddg 0". Thirty blows at 255% hit and 255% crit is not a number, it is uninitialised bytes in the BattleUnit struct being formatted as if it were a real forecast — the struct is only populated for a side that actually fights, and the no-counter case leaves it stale. CLAUDE.md's own rule is "report raw facts alongside interpretations"; here a sentinel is dressed up as an interpretation, and a caller who trusted it would read a 255% crit as certain death and retreat a unit that was in no danger at all. Same shape as the turn-3 forecast/act contradiction: the forecast layer does not distinguish "this side fights" from "this side does not".
wanted: Detect the no-counter case (defender's equipped weapon range does not contain the combat distance, or defender blows == 0) and print "defender: cannot counter (Iron Bow 2-2 at range 1)" instead of formatting the stale struct. Failing that, sanity-clamp and flag anything out of range — hit and crit above 100, blows above 4 — as "STALE/INVALID" rather than printing it as data. Worth applying to fe7_forecast too, since it reads the same structs.

Plus fe7_convoy({action:'list'|'withdraw'|'deposit', item_slot}) when standing next to Merlinus. Both are P0 for a defend chapter, where the whole game is HP throughput across a rotation.

detail: Turn 7. I used fe7_act(action:'seize') on Hector at (12,1) purely as a probe — its documented behaviour is to report the menu and press nothing, which makes it the only safe way to see what commands exist. It returned: "the menu holds [0x8b9559c, item, trade, wait]". Three of four named; the first is a bare pointer. So I dumped the table from ROM. It is a clean array: base 0x08b95314, stride 0x24, EXACTLY 27 entries (index 0..26) terminated by an all-zero entry at 0x08b956e0, and every entry carries a name text ID at +0x00 and a description text ID at +0x02 (all 0x81c). index = (ptr - 0x08b95314) / 0x24. Known anchors: idx0 seize (name 0x3f94), idx1 attack (0x3f8c), idx22 item (0x3ec4), idx23 trade (0x3ebc), idx26 wait (0x3ea0). The unnamed entry Hector had is idx18, name text ID 0x3ef4. Given it appeared only with four allies adjacent and sits four slots before Item, alongside idx19/20/21 (0x3ee8/0x3edc/0x3ed0), it is very probably Rescue with Take/Drop/Give around it — but I am NOT asserting that, because "location is not semantics" and I have not tested it by effect. What I can assert: src/fe7.ts:776 MENU_CMD hardcodes 5 of 27 commands, so 22 of the game's own unit actions are invisible to the tool layer and unreachable through it. Notably idx1 and idx2 share the same name ID 0x3f8c and the same +0x04 word, i.e. there are two distinct Attack-family entries — a detail that would matter to any code deriving the Attack index.</detail>
wanted: Decode the +0x00 name text ID through the text decoder the tools already have (the same one that reads 0x0202A5B4 for fe7_unstick's text buffer) and build MENU_CMD from ROM at startup instead of hardcoding 5 pointers — the table is self-terminating, so this is a loop, not a transcription. Then fe7_act can (a) name every entry it reports, which turns "[0x8b9559c, item, trade, wait]" into a usable answer, and (b) offer a generic fe7_act({action:'menu', command:'rescue'|'visit'|'door'|'chest'|...}) that derives the index by pointer the way 'seize' already does, rather than needing a new hand-written action per command. That single change unblocks rescue, trade, visit, door, chest, steal, talk and dance at once.

Walking the cursor over my own units returned "Hector", "Eliwood.", "Lyn.", "Marcus", "Lucius", "Bartre", "Florina.", "Legault.", "Sain", "Raven.", "Priscilla.", "Merlinus", "Isadora." and green "Nils" — one call, thirteen tiles. fe7_state gives me "#9 cls0C Lv1 (10,3) HP37/37" for that same unit. detail: Turn 8. I probed fe7_act with a destination occupied by an enemy: Isadora (#29) at (9,2) -> (10,4), where enemy #1 (cls12, 8/29) is standing, a tile 3 cost away and well inside her Move 8. Result: "Destination (10,4) is NOT reachable for unit #29 (grid = 0xFF: out of range, or blocked terrain). Move cancelled." Compare the green-unit case on turn 4, which said "OCCUPIED by a green unit (slot #0, cls49, HP 10/10)" — faction, slot, class and HP. The enemy case names none of it and offers two guesses, neither of which is the truth: the tile is in range and the terrain is Floor, an enemy is simply on it. fe7_act already reads all three unit arrays to produce the green message, so the enemy is one lookup away. Related documentation defect: fe7_reachable's legend reads "digits = move cost (legal stop), U = ally, G = green NPC, E = enemy (all pass-through only)". Allies and greens genuinely are pass-through; enemies are NOT — they block pathing outright in FE7, which is exactly why this tile reads 0xFF rather than a cost. Grouping all three under "pass-through only" states something false about the case that matters most for routing.</detail>
wanted: When the cost grid reads 0xFF, cross-check the occupancy layer at 0x0202E3DC before reporting, and say "an enemy is standing there (slot #1, cls12, 8/29) — enemies block pathing, so this tile and anything behind it is unreachable" instead of "out of range, or blocked terrain". Distinguish the three real causes: out of Move, impassable terrain for this unit's movement class, or blocked by an enemy. And fix fe7_reachable's legend to say enemies BLOCK while allies and greens are pass-through-but-not-stoppable.

detail: CHAPTER LOST, turn 8 enemy phase. Nils died; text buffer ".A..I'm sorry....Ninian...........Nils!!." and the screen is GAME OVER. Sequence: Raven (#9) was rotated into the wall tile (10,3) at 37/37 full HP, dropped to 21/37 by the time fe7_end_turn's 12s summary printed, then FELL later in the same enemy phase; with (10,3) empty the corridor into Nils's sealed room was open and later-acting enemies walked through (10,3)->(10,2)->(10,1) and killed a 10 HP green NPC. Twelve of my thirteen units were alive and three of them were at 29/36, 29/40 and 29/37 — the chapter was not lost to attrition, it was lost in a single phase to one tile opening. THIS IS THE THREAT-RANGE GAP FROM MY TURN-2 NOTE, cashed in. I had no way to ask "how much damage can reach (10,3) next phase" and no way to ask "if that unit dies mid-phase, who can then reach (10,1)". I sized the wall by looking at last phase's damage — 11 on turn 7, 8 on turn 6 — which is exactly the sampling error RAM.md's method notes warn about: the phase before, Marcus had taken 35 in one go. A wall unit with 37 HP was therefore never safe, and nothing in the tool layer would tell me that. The defend objective makes it strictly worse than a normal map: on a rout map a dead wall unit costs you a unit, here it costs the chapter instantly, because the thing behind the wall has 10 HP and moves on its own.</detail>
wanted: The threat overlay from the turn-2 note, but specifically two things it must answer: (a) fe7_threat({tile}) -> the list of enemies that can reach a weapon-range tile of it, with each one's forecast damage and hit%, so "can my wall unit survive the phase" is a sum I can read rather than a guess; (b) a second-order version that answers "if the unit on tile T dies, what becomes reachable" — because on a chokepoint defend map the failure mode is not gradual, it is a single tile flipping from blocked to open mid-phase. Even a crude version (flood-fill the terrain-cost layer from every enemy, ignore ordering) would have told me a 37 HP unit was inside a 40+ damage envelope.

detail: fe7_wait DOES NOT DETECT GAME OVER. After Nils died I called fe7_wait three times; each returned "Still enemy phase after 90s (turn 8). A was pressed throughout, so a dialogue box is not what's holding it. Call fe7_wait again to keep waiting." — a total of 4.5 minutes of polling a game that had already ended, with the tool actively instructing me to keep waiting. The state it printed contained the answer twice over and did not act on it: "players 12 alive, FALLEN: #9 cls0C" and, on the very next call, "green 0" — the green array going from 1 to 0 on a chapter whose objective is to defend a green NPC IS the loss condition, and the tool reported it as a bare count with no comment. I only found out by calling fe7_unstick, whose screenshot said GAME OVER and whose text buffer held Nils's death quote. Note the phase byte still read 0x80 (enemy), so phase polling alone will never terminate. Two smaller things in the same lines: the fallen unit is reported as "#9 cls0C" rather than "Raven", and fe7_end_turn's 12s summary had shown Raven at 21/37 — alive — so the last information I had before the loss was reassuring and stale.</detail>
wanted: fe7_wait (and fe7_end_turn) must check for the game-over/defeat state each poll and return immediately with "CHAPTER LOST — <reason>" instead of advising another wait. Cheap detectors, any one of which would have caught this: the text buffer containing a lord/objective death quote, the green array emptying on a defend chapter, a lord's HP hitting 0, or whatever flag the GAME OVER screen sets. It should also name fallen units and explicitly flag whether the fallen unit was a lord or the objective unit, since those end the run and every other death does not.
